title: Indian National Tushar Sharma, 25, Found Dead in Burning Car in Langley
excerpt: British Columbia homicide investigators say the evidence suggests the Surrey resident was targeted. No suspect has been named, and police are appealing for information about his movements before October 29.
body:
• British Columbia homicide investigators have identified the man found dead in a burning vehicle in Langley on October 29 as Tushar Sharma, 25, of Surrey, releasing his name and photograph on November 17 to advance the case.
  • Investigators say the evidence gathered so far suggests Sharma was targeted. The motive remains unknown and police have not publicly identified any suspect.
  • Sharma had no criminal record and had limited known contacts in Canada, according to the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT).
  • Anyone who knew Sharma or saw anything connected to the Rawlinson Crescent fire on October 29 can contact IHIT at 1-877-551-4448 or ihitinfo@rcmp-grc.gc.ca, quoting file 2026-1052.

Canadian homicide investigators have identified the victim found inside a burning car in Langley, British Columbia, last month as Tushar Sharma, a 25-year-old Indian national who lived in Surrey. The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) released Sharma's name and photograph on November 17, 2026, and said the evidence gathered so far suggests he was deliberately targeted.

What happened on October 29

The investigation began at approximately 10:26 p.m. on October 29, 2026, when Langley RCMP responded to a report of a vehicle fire in the 23300-block of Rawlinson Crescent in Langley. Firefighters from the Township of Langley Fire Department attended with RCMP officers, and while extinguishing the fire they discovered what appeared to be human remains inside the vehicle.

IHIT, the regional homicide team for communities policed by the RCMP across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley, has assumed conduct of the investigation. It is working with Langley RCMP, the Integrated Forensic Identification Services and the BC Coroners Service to establish the circumstances surrounding Sharma's death, and investigators have been piecing together a timeline of events leading up to the fire.

"While the motive remains under investigation, evidence to date suggests this was a targeted incident."

— Sgt. Freda Fong, Integrated Homicide Investigation Team

A victim with few local ties

According to IHIT, Sharma did not have a criminal record and had limited known contacts in Canada. Sergeant Freda Fong said investigators are speaking with Sharma's family and friends in Canada and overseas to build a picture of his lifestyle and activities before his death. Because Sharma lived in Surrey, investigators hope people in Surrey, Langley and across the region who knew him — or who saw anything connected to the fire — will recognize his photograph and come forward.

Police have not publicly identified any suspect, and no motive has been established. Zee News, reporting the identification on November 19, said investigators are also working to establish how many people may have been involved and why the vehicle was set on fire.

How to help the investigation

IHIT is asking anyone with information about this investigation to contact the team at 1-877-551-IHIT (4448) or by email at ihitinfo@rcmp-grc.gc.ca, quoting IHIT file 2026-1052. Investigators are particularly interested in Sharma's movements and activities before October 29 and in anything seen near Rawlinson Crescent on the night of the fire.

For Surrey and Langley's large South Asian community, the appeal is the story for now: a 25-year-old who had built few ties in Canada was found dead in circumstances police describe as targeted, and the people most likely to hold the missing pieces are those who crossed his path in the region. The investigation remains ongoing.
